cumleler: How is a tiny ear sound separated from a huge echo?
Transient-evoked otoacoustic emissions, or TEOAE, are recorded with clicks.
In this protocol, clicks come in groups of four; three match.
The fourth click is reversed and three times stronger.
Added together, the linear ear canal echo largely cancels out.
The cochlear emission does not grow linearly, so part of it remains.
